thread:
alex: RFC follow-up — proposing we extract tenant policy + runtime rule evaluation into a tiny, well-defined 'policy-spine' service that both control-plane and the runtime call. sketch: https://drive.redwood/policy-spine-sketch

rachel: quick q — is this primarily to stop duplication (control-plane <> runtime) or to enable faster rule iteration?

alex: both. duplication causes drift (we've hotfixed twice this quarter). also gives us a single source for tenant-level feature flags and rate rules so rollouts are consistent. main concerns: latency in hot path and ownership between infra vs platform.

jamal: latency is my biggest worry. runtime does check-per-token for some auth features. How would we keep latencies sub-ms?

maya: can we keep a local cache (prefix/KV) in runtime and have the policy-spine as authoritative async source? fallback to cached rules on miss/timeout.

alex: exactly. proposal = authoritative store + push-based watch to runtimes for hot rule updates. runtime keeps bounded LRU and applies quick checks locally. policy-spine publishes invalidations.

tony: DB migration note: current tenant rules live in config-db (monolith). moving to a new store means migrating >20k rows and preserving audit history. Plan?

alex: migrate in-place: keep a read-replica forwarder that writes to both stores for N weeks, run diffs daily, then cut reads over by flag per-tenant. we'll keep audit log pointers, no schema change for rules initially.

emily: can we avoid schema changes by storing serialized RuleSet in a v1 column in the new service and add parsed fields later? saves product changes.

nina: operational testing — we should create load tests that simulate 5k tps of rule lookups with ~95% cache hit. measure 95th/99th tail before canary. Also add regression evals to ensure correctness for edge rule combos.

jamal: also need SRE/ops runbook. If policy-spine is down, runtime must degrade gracefully — i.e., use last-known rules, and if none present, use tenant-default-permissions. Add alerts for cache-staleness.

alex: agreed. ownership proposal: infra builds the service (db+kafka+api), platform owns schema/compat and migration + tests, SRE owns runbook and alerts. Will add explicit RACI.

rachel: how about the API contract? keep it tiny. example:

```
// PolicyStore contract v1
getTenantRules(tenantId) -> RuleSet
watch(tenantId) -> stream(invalidation)
getDelta(sinceCursor) -> [Change]
```

maya: +1, keep it idempotent and versioned. add a read header: X-Policy-Version so runtime can validate cache coherence.

tony: cutover strategy idea: canary by tenant group (internal -> small customers -> wide). feature flag: policy-spine-enabled per-tenant. Also a compatibility shim in runtime for a few months.

alex: migration timeline draft:
- week 0: build service + dual-write forwarder
- week 2: smoke + e2e tests
- week 3: internal canary (10 tenants)
- week 5: 1% production canary, run load tests
- week 8: ramp using success gates (latency/regression)

nina: add a KPI: token latency delta <= 1ms p95, error budget burn <2% during canary.

deploy-bot: deploy #policy-spine:staging succeeded (build 0.8.1) :rocket:

alex: next steps — I'll open an RFC follow-up doc with diagrams + RACI + migration playbook. please drop concerns here. if no blockers by EOD Fri we'll sync up with infra and SRE to schedule the first spike. :thumbsup:

jamal: fine for me, want to check cache invalidation corner cases in spike.

emily: I'll own the feature-flagging plumbing and rollout dashboard.

rachel: can we add a short privacy review? tenant rules include PII-style identifiers in some rules.

alex: noted — pinging @security for a quick pass after RFC doc.

maya: one more ops ask — add a /metrics endpoint exposing cache_hit_ratio, staleness_ms, last_sync_cursor. that will make SLOs easy.

alex: yep. adding metrics and health endpoints to the checklist. thanks all.
